title: What modernism changed: how writers broke the old forms, 1900 to 1940
examples: What are the features of modernist writing?

explain.say: Virginia Woolf once wrote, half joking, that on or about December 1910 human character changed. She meant that writers suddenly felt the old ways of telling stories no longer fitted modern life. The board compares the Victorian novel with what replaced it: modernism, roughly 1900 to 1940.

draw.text: What modernism changed: how writers broke the old forms, 1900 to 1940

explain.say: Why the change? Look at the causes. The First World War killed millions and shattered faith in progress. Freud argued the mind has hidden depths. Cities filled with cars, cinema and telephones, and Einstein made even time relative. If your world felt broken and fast, what kind of story would you write?

explain.say: Sort the new tools. Some go inside the mind, like stream of consciousness, which follows thoughts as they flow. Some break the shape, with fragments and collage, like a cubist painting. In poetry, Ezra Pound and the Imagists wanted sharp, clear images in free verse, which has no fixed metre. Which tool would you try first?

Follow the timeline. 1922 was the big year: James Joyce's Ulysses and T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land both appeared. Modernism was international too: in Harlem, Black writers remade American poetry, and writers in Paris, Dublin, London and New York borrowed from each other. Which of these have you met?

explain.say: So here is the change in one picture. On the left, the Victorian novel, with a confident narrator guiding you. On the right, modernism, which asks you, the reader, to piece the meaning together. Pound's slogan was make it new. Great work. Challenge: retell a fairy tale in fragments from three characters' minds.

faq.a: A movement from roughly 1900 to 1940 in which writers broke with Victorian conventions, experimenting with fragmented form, stream of consciousness, free verse and multiple viewpoints to capture modern life and the inner mind.

Many pressures at once: the trauma of the First World War, Freud's psychology, Einstein's physics, fast-growing cities and new technologies like cinema. Writers felt the old forms could not express this new world.

faq.q: What are the features of modernist writing?
faq.a: Fragmentation, stream of consciousness, shifting or unreliable viewpoints, allusion and myth, open endings, and in poetry free verse and sharp images. The reader is asked to work out meaning.

faq.q: Why is 1922 called the year of modernism?
faq.a: Joyce's Ulysses, Eliot's The Waste Land and Woolf's Jacob's Room all appeared that year, so critics often call 1922 modernism's annus mirabilis, or wonderful year.
A poetry movement around 1912 to 1917, led by Ezra Pound, H.D. and Amy Lowell, that demanded direct treatment of the thing, no wasted words, and the rhythm of natural speech rather than fixed metre.

facts: James Joyce's Ulysses and T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land were both published in 1922.
Woolf's remark about December 1910 comes from her 1924 essay Mr Bennett and Mrs Brown.
Make It New is the title of Ezra Pound's 1934 essay collection.
